{{ill|Shinkai Sansha Shrine|ja|新海三社神社|qid=Q22119059}} is a regional {{ill|Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine|en}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shinkaisansya-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.guidoor.jp/en/places/3414|access-date=2023-11-01|website=Guidoor|language=en}}</ref> in {{ill|Minamisaku District, Nagano|ceb|Minamisaku-gun|de|Minamisaku-gun|fi|Minami-Sakun piirikunta|fr|District de Minamisaku|id|Distrik Minamisaku, Nagano|it|Distretto di Minamisaku|ja|南佐久郡|ko|미나미사쿠군|pl|Powiat Minamisaku|uk|Повіт Мінамі-Саку|zh|南佐久郡|qid=Q1154776}} {{ill|Kitasaku District, Nagano|ceb|Kitasaku-gun|de|Kitasaku-gun|fi|Kita-Sakun piirikunta|fr|District de Kitasaku|it|Distretto di Kitasaku|ja|北佐久郡|ko|기타사쿠군|pl|Powiat Kitasaku|uk|Повіт Кіта-Саку|zh|北佐久郡|qid=Q1142451}} {{ill|Chiisagata District, Nagano|en|Chiisagata District, Nagano|qid=Q1072595|lt=Chiisagata District, Nagano}} It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

'''Shinkai Sansha Shrine''' (also simply called " '''Shinkai Shrine''' ") is {{ill|Shinto shrine|a shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Taguchi|11=田口村_(長野県)|Taguchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17175714}}, {{ill|Saku, Nagano|ar|ساكو (ناغانو)|azb|ساکو، ناقانو|be|Саку (горад)|ce|Саку (гӀала)|ceb|Saku (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Saku (Nagano)|de|Saku (Nagano)|eo|Saku|es|Saku (Nagano)|et|Saku (Jaapan)|fa|ساکو، ناگانو|fi|Saku (Nagano)|fr|Saku (Japon)|gl|Saku|hy|Սակու (քաղաք)|id|Saku, Nagano|it|Saku (Giappone)|ja|佐久市|ko|사쿠시|mzn|ساکو، ناگانو|nl|Saku (Nagano)|pl|Saku (miasto)|pt|Saku (Nagano)|ro|Saku|ru|Саку (город)|sh|Saku|sr|Саку (Јапан)|sv|Saku, Nagano|tg|Саку|th|ซากุ|tl|Saku, Nagano|tr|Saku, Nagano|tt|Саку (шәһәр)|uk|Саку (Наґано)|ur|ساکو، ناگانو|vi|Saku, Nagano|war|Saku, Nagano|zh|佐久市|zh_classical|佐久市|zh_min_nan|Saku-chhī|zh_yue|佐久|qid=Q495821|lt=Saku, Nagano}}. It was a former prefectural shrine and {{ill|Sōja shrine|the main shrine|en}} of {{ill|Saku District, Shinano|en|Saku District, Shinano|qid=Q7403130|lt=Saku District}} . The {{ill|Saijin|en|Saijin|lt=Enshrined deities}} are {{ill|Okihagi no Mikoto|en|Okihagi no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi no Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshironushi|qq=}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|en|Emperor Ōjin|lt=Homudawake no Mikoto}} . {{ill|Mon (emblem)|en|Mon (emblem)|qid=Q600964|lt=The sacred crest}} is {{ill|the Kaji leaf|en|the Kaji leaf}} . The founding date is unknown.

== Overview ==
The main enshrined deity, {{ill|Okihagi|en|Okihagi|lt=Okihagi-no-Mikoto}}, is the grandson of the Great God [[Ōkuninushi]] from [[Izumo-taisha]] and the god of development in Saku. Okihagi-no-Mikoto's father is {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}} from [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Taisha]], and his mother is {{ill|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami|en|Ueno Nukisaki no Megami}} ({{ill|Arafune Daimyojin|en|Arafune Daimyojin}}). Within the shrine grounds and nearby, there's a group of ancient Kofuns known as the "Forty-Eight Tombs," which some believe are remnants of ancient religious practices. The Shinkai Sansha Shrine, which was considered a "Prefectural Shrine" (Ken-sha) during the [[Kofun period]], came under the influence of Suwa gods during the samurai era and had a powerful domain stretching from Saku to Ueda. Additionally, Shinkai Sansha Shrine is also known as Saku Shrine or Kai Shrine, with the latter name originating from Okihagi-no-Mikoto being the ancestral god of Saku's development. The "{{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|En|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba}}" from the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}} introduces it as "Nīzaku-no-Kami."

During the Sengoku period, Takeda Shingen prayed for victory and donated a sword, reportedly restoring the shrine's buildings, and the prayer certificate still remains.<ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> In the Edo period, a debate arose over which shrine should be considered the primary one in Saku since Shinkai Sansha Shrine wasn't included among the recognized sites, sparking controversy. During the early Meiji period's separation of Shinto and Buddhism, the three-storied pagoda (which was part of the temple complex Shinkaisan Kamiyama Gongan-in Jingūmitsudera) was to be destroyed, but the shrine argued it was not a pagoda but a treasure house, and that was accepted. The pagoda from the Muromachi period still stands on the shrine grounds. Before World War II, the Shinkai Sansha Shrine's grand procession was held, where priests on horseback paraded through the South and North Saku to the Oagata District.<ref>『佐久の神社と信仰』信濃教育出版部、1989th year 、261頁。</ref>

== Cultural Assets ==

=== Important Cultural Property (nationally designated) ===

* Three-storied pagodas - Built in the late Muromachi period (1515). A three-bay, three-story pagoda with a shingled roof. Designated on August 28, 1907 (Meiji 40). <ref name="#1">『神社考』双葉印刷、1984th year 、全304頁</ref>
* East Main Shrine - Built in the late Muromachi period (1467-1572). The one-bay, Nagare-zukuri style shrine has a cypress bark roof. Designated on July 29, 1937. <ref name="#1" /> Enshrining the chief deity, Okinawa no Mikoto

== Shrine precincts ==

* {{ill|Kinugasa Shrine|en|Kinugasa Shrine}}
* {{ill|Fukuda Inari Shrine|en|Fukuda Inari Shrine}}

In addition, there is a joint hall for 12 eastern and western sub-shrines. Next to the {{ill|Torii|the torii gate|en}} stands the largest tree in the shrine grounds, a large zelkova tree said to be over 1,000 years old. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref>

== Sacred Tree ==
[[File:Shinkai_Sansha_Jinja_map.png|thumb| The sacred cedar tree and the zelkova tree near the torii gate]]
There is a {{ill|Shinboku|There is a sacred|en}} {{ill|Cryptomeria|ar|سرو اليابان|arz|سرو اليابان|az|Yapon kriptomeriyası|ca|Criptomèria|ceb|Cryptomeria japonica|cs|Kryptomerie japonská|da|Japansk kryptomeria|de|Sicheltanne|dsb|Japańska kryptomerija|el|Ιαπωνικό κυπαρίσσι|eo|Sugio|es|Cryptomeria japonica|eu|Japoniar zedro|fa|سدر ژاپنی|fi|Sugi|fr|Cryptomeria japonica|frr|Cryptomeria japonica|ga|Céadar Seapánach|gl|Criptomeria|he|קריפטומריה|hr|Japanska kriptomerija|hsb|Japanska kryptomerija|hu|Japánciprus|hy|Կրիպտոմերիա ճապոնական|is|Keisaraviður|it|Cryptomeria japonica|ja|スギ|ka|იაპონური კრიპტომერია|ko|삼나무|koi|Криптомерия|kv|Криптомерия|lt|Japoninė kriptomerija|mrj|Криптомери|ne|धुपी सल्ला|nl|Sikkelcipres|no|Japanseder|pl|Kryptomeria japońska|pms|Cryptomeria japonica|pt|Cryptomeria japonica|ro|Criptomeria|ru|Криптомерия|sl|Japonska kriptomerija|su|Cedar Jepang|sv|Kryptomeria|tr|Japon çamı|udm|Криптомерия|uk|Криптомерія японська|vi|Liễu sam|war|Cryptomeria japonica|zh|日本柳杉|qid=Q147388|lt=Cryptomeria}} tree about 20 meters in front of the east main hall. Its age is unknown, but as of 1940 it was over 30 metres tall, 12 metres thick at the base, and 8 metres at its diameter. <ref name="nagano">[https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1115449/57 県社新海三社神社御神木杉]『[長野県]史蹟名勝天然紀念物調査報告. 第21輯』長野県、1940</ref> When {{ill|Nio (Buddhism)|en|Nio (Buddhism)|qid=Q539715|lt=the Niomon Gate}} burned down in the early Meiji period, the fire spread to the base of the temple, and all {{ill|Ujigami|the parishioners|en}} gathered together and spent several days extinguishing the fire. Before the war, when the trunk of the tree began to lean severely, they received guidance from Dr. {{ill|Honda Seiroku|11=本多静六|Honda Seiroku|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11520098}}, a doctor of {{ill|Doctor of Philosophy in Forestry|11=博士（林学）|forestry|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q98117672}} and had it reinforced with donations from all the parishioners. <ref name="nagano" />

== Anecdote ==

* The road taken during the divine procession was called "Shinkaido" and {{ill|Shinko-shiki|the divine procession|en}} itself was called " {{ill|gokou|11=御幸|Miyuki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q16280183}} " <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 北佐久篇』7ページ。</ref> .
* Behind the shrine is Yoshiike Pond. Long ago, a monk learned of this pond after hearing a prophecy from a snake. It is said that when a monk ground ink in the water of the pond and wrote Sanskrit characters, the characters were reflected on 36 sheets of paper below, and so the Goshintomi Festival began. It was also said that anyone who saw a Shinto priest wearing a white mask going to fetch water in the middle of the night would suffer misfortune, so villagers would go to bed early. <ref>『限定復刻版 佐久口碑伝説集 南佐久篇』121ページ。</ref>
* {{ill|Mayor of Saku City|en|Mayor of Saku City}}, {{ill|Seiji Yanagida|11=柳田清二|Seiji Yanagida|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/10=ja|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17222140}}, spoke about the anime film " {{ill|Your Name|Your Name."|en}} Since it has been introduced as a sacred place for the movie, some people visit the area to verify the location or make a pilgrimage there. <ref>[https://twitter.com/Seiji_Ya/status/771939265534132224 【君の名は。『聖地』新海三社神社】]佐久市長柳田清二Twitter, 2016.9.3</ref>
